content: 1. Ethinyl estradiol metabolism may be increased, potentially reducing its effectiveness. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider using an additional non-hormonal contraceptive method for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unknown but may involve ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 2. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases everolimus levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 3. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases felodipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the felodipine dose by 50% during coadministration and for three days after the last nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dose. 4. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fentanyl levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Careful monitoring of fentanyl’s therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression, is recommended. Reduce the fentanyl dose if necessary. 5. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases finerenone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elevated finerenone concentrations may increase the risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and hyponatremia. 6. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases flecainide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases flibanserin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elevated flibanserin concentrations may increase the risk of hypotension, syncope, and central nervous system depression. 8. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fluticasone furoate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids such as beclomethasone or prednisolone. 9. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fosamprenavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events related to nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 10. Fosphenytoin decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Do not initiate nirmatrelvir/ritonavir immediately after discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inducer due to the time required for systemic clearance. 11. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases futibatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 12. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases gepirone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Serum concentrations of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase due to P-gp, BCRP, and OATP1B inhibition by ritonavir. 14. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases hydrocodone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Careful monitoring of hydrocodone’s therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression, is recommended. Reduce the hydrocodone dose if necessary. 15. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ibrutinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases indinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events related to nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or protease inhibitors. 17. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases irbesartan levels or effects by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 18. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases itraconazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Limit the itraconazole adult dose to 200 mg/day if coadministered with ritonavir. 20. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivabradine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elevated ivabradine concentrations may increase the risk of bradycardia or conduction disturbances. 21. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivacaftor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the dosage of ivacaftor, elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor, or tezacaftor/ivacaftor if coadministered. 22. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivosidenib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration due to the potential risk of serious adverse events, such as QT interval prolongation. 23. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ketoconazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Limit the ketoconazole adult dose to 200 mg/day if coadministered with ritonavir. 24. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases labetalol levels or effects by inducing UGT2B7 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 25. Lenacapavir increases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 26. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases leniolisib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases levoketoconazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Limit the ketoconazole adult dose to 200 mg/day if coadministered with ritonavir. 28. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lidocaine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor lidocaine therapeutic concentrations if available. 29. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lomitapide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elevated lomitapide concentrations may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity and gastrointestinal effects. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases losartan levels or effects by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. No dosage adjustment is required. 31. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lovastatin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Discontinue lovastatin at least 12 hours before initiating nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and for five days after completing treatment. 32. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 33. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lumateperone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Limit the dose to 5 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lurasidone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lurbinectedin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, increase the lurbinectedin dose to the pre-coadministration level. 36. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases macitentan levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. No dosage adjustment is required. 37. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases maraviroc levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases mavacamten levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Elevated mavacamten concentrations may result in heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 39. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases mavorixafor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the daily dose of mavorixafor with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases meperidine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases methadone levels or effects by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Methadone is metabolized by CYP2B6 and CYP3A4. Ritonavir may decrease methadone exposure through CYP2B6 induction, partially offset by CYP3A4 inhibition. 42. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases methylergonovine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases methylprednisolone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression.
